rows.grounds: bahuvrīhi compound kṛta-pratisara qualifying the summoned king; pratisara denotes a protective ritual thread or amulet
adjective qualifying the summoned king, indicating a calm ritual disposition
final member of compound khaḍga-kheṭaka-dhāriṇām, denoting those who bear sword and shield

items.question: What ritual condition and armed accompaniment must characterize the summoned king?
premises: The summoned king is described as having made a protective thread.
The summoned king is described as peaceful in disposition.
The context includes bearers of sword and shield.
items.inference: The king must be ritually prepared with a protective thread and calm demeanor in the presence of armed attendants.
uncertainties: Whether khaḍga-kheṭaka-dhāriṇām qualifies attendants accompanying the king or another group present is not explicit.
items.plain_english: Having summoned the king, who has made the protective thread and is peaceful, in the presence of those bearing sword and shield.
